items.prompt: Black to move. In our data 14 of 27 players under 1500 jumped the knight to b4 here, and 13 chose another square. Find a good square for the attacked knight.

claims.statement: Nb8 and Ne5 are within 40 centipawns of the best move.
Nb4 is at least 250 centipawns worse.

hints: The knight on c6 is attacked by a pawn.
After Nb4, White has a queen check that attacks the knight too.
Retreat to b8 or jump to e5.
items.explain: Nb4 meets a queen check and loses material; the retreat or the jump to e5 keeps the balance.

feedback_by_move.c6b4: The knight steps to a square where a queen check wins time and material. Chosen by 14 of 27 players under 1500 in our data [V].

items.prompt: Black to move. Queen on e6, White's pieces developing. In our data 18 of 44 players under 1500 moved the queen to g6. Find a good move (several work).

claims.statement: Qd7, Nf6 and Qd6 are within 40 centipawns of the best move.
Qg6 is at least 100 centipawns worse.

hints: Which squares can White's knight and pawns attack next?
Think about what White's knight can do from b5.
Retreat the queen to d7, or develop the knight.
items.explain: Qd7, Nf6 and Qd6 are close in value. Qg6 loses at least 100 centipawns, because a knight jump to b5 makes threats.

feedback_by_move.e6g6: The queen goes to a square where a knight jump to b5 creates threats. Chosen by 18 of 44 players under 1500 in our data [V].

items.prompt: Black to move. The bishop on h5 is attacked by a pawn. Find a safe reply.

claims.statement: Bg6 is the engine's choice at depth 16.
b5 is at least 100 centipawns worse.
Nxg4 is at least 150 centipawns worse.

hints: List the squares the bishop can reach, then check what each allows.
Capturing on g4 loses material to a recapture.
The bishop retreats along its diagonal.
items.explain: Bg6 is the only reply within 100 centipawns of the best; b5 and Nxg4 cost much more.

items.prompt: Black to move. Name any one reply that keeps the position balanced.

claims.statement: Four replies are within 40 centipawns of the best.

hints: There is not just one answer.
Think about developing or moving the queen.
The knight on b8 or the queen can move.
items.explain: Four different replies are all within 40 centipawns of the best, so Black can afford a loose move here.

items.prompt: Black just chose Nc6 here. What kind of mistake is it?

options: missed a better capture or check

claims.statement: After Nc6 the black loose pieces are exactly these.

hints: Look at the knight you just moved: who attacks it, and who defends it?
Count attackers and defenders of the piece on c6.
The moved piece is attacked and has no defender.
items.explain: After Nc6, a piece is left attacked and undefended, and the move loses at least 250 centipawns.

answer.class: missed a better capture or check
options: missed a better capture or check

claims.statement: After Qe7 the black loose pieces are exactly these.
Qe7 is at least 250 centipawns worse than the best move.
The engine's choice is a capture.

options: missed a better capture or check

claims.statement: After Nc6 the black loose pieces are exactly these.
Nc6 is at least 250 centipawns worse than the best move.
The engine's choice is a quiet move.
The best move's target square holds nothing (a quiet move).

hints: Nothing is left loose after the move. Look for a better move.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a safe move.

claims.statement: Bd3 is the engine's choice.
Ng3 is at least 700 centipawns worse.

hints: List every capture and check Black has after your move.
What is the knight standing in front of?
Block the diagonal with another piece.
items.explain: Ng3 uncovers the black queen's attack on the undefended white queen; Bd3 blocks it.

claims.statement: Kxd7 is the engine's choice.
Rxd7 is at least 700 centipawns worse.

hints: Two pieces can take the queen. What is each doing now?
Think about which pieces defend which.
Capture with the king.
items.explain: Rxd7 removes the defender of the rook on f8; the king capture keeps both rooks defended.

items.prompt: Black to move and well ahead. The knight on b8 is attacked. Find a safe move that keeps the advantage.

claims.statement: Nd7, Ke7 and Qh2 are within 110 centipawns of the best.
Qb7 is at least 900 centipawns worse.

hints: List every check White has after your move.
Where can the white knight on c4 jump with check?
Move the knight out of attack, or move the king.
items.explain: Qb7 allows a knight check that forks the king and the queen; the three listed moves keep the advantage.

items.prompt: Black to move after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 f6 (a pawn move) 3.Nc3. In our data the pawn to c6 was the most common choice under 1500 (14 of 42). Find the engine's choice.

claims.statement: Nc6 is the engine's choice.
c6 is at least 60 centipawns worse.

hints: Which piece can defend the e5 pawn?
The pawn on c7 blocks the knight's best square.
Develop the knight to c6.
items.explain: c6 loses at least 60 centipawns and allows a strong knight capture on e5; Nc6 defends the pawn.

feedback_by_move.c7c6: The pawn takes the knight's natural square and leaves e5 weak. Chosen by 14 of 42 players under 1500 in our data [V].
